# North Shelf: where your 40 water-treatment kits stand

## 1. The request and the count

Field Clinic S-3 asked Harbor Depot for 40 water-treatment kits under North Shelf. The request is for 40 water-treatment kits, and it's on file. The clinic's water point uses about 20 kits a week, according to the request record. A request on file doesn't schedule a pickup or a delivery, and there is no delivery date.

Harbor Depot has 27 water-treatment kits counted and staged in pen 4. Every kit is sealed, and no carton is damaged. That count is custody, not a release. It also leaves a gap: 27 on hand doesn't fill a request for 40.

## 2. Your five questions

1. How many kits, and when? We hold 27 water-treatment kits, and none can be sent yet, because no lot is released. No arrival date exists, and the release desk does not give release dates in advance.
2. The other 13? The sources don't say when, or whether, more kits will come.
3. Your own vehicle during the documentation window? No. The window is for paperwork questions, and the clinic must not send a vehicle to collect kits.
4. Release timing? The release desk tells the Field Clinic S-3 supply clerk directly when it records a release. No one can give a date before then.
5. Patients? Don't tell patients that treatment water is coming. The sources give nothing else to say to them.

## 3. How a release happens, and who owns it

Three offices act before a release exists. The release desk releases a lot. The transport desk assigns a vehicle. The permit office approves a permit. Only when all three are done does the release desk record a release.

Ivo Marsh at the Harbor Depot release desk owns any release. Neither the inventory clerk nor the Field Clinic S-3 supply clerk owns it.

## 4. What hasn't happened

No lot has been released. No vehicle has been assigned. No permit has been approved. No receipt has been confirmed. Whether the movement is supportable is unknown.

You may see truck HS-3 parked in bay 2. HS-3 isn't assigned to any request. The yard board shows where vehicles are parked; it doesn't assign them.

## 5. Hold these actions

Until a release is recorded, the clinic must not:

- schedule kit use;
- tell patients that treatment water is coming;
- send a vehicle to collect kits;
- treat the documentation window as a time the kits will arrive.

The clinic should not treat the filed request as a pickup appointment or a delivery date either. Counted kits in pen 4 are in custody; they aren't on their way.

## 6. Paperwork questions

Call 555-0194 with paperwork questions during the documentation window, Thursday and Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Calls outside the window are not answered. Good paperwork questions include a correction to the request record or a question about the count sheet. The window isn't a pickup appointment, a dispatch, or a delivery promise.

This brief is for the Field Clinic S-3 supply team.
